# the contributor audit: finite reflection flatness and scalar crossover

## Nonsymmetric flat source

The root fully read `candidate d896994f234b7b69`
and ran its standard-library verifier: PASS.

The midpoint hexagon satisfies all three displayed middle-triangle facets,
with a distinct active contact on each. The endpoint pair and the middle
triangle consequently are the exact integer fibers of their hull. The
middle triangle is not centrally symmetric. Each of the three explicitly
given involutions permutes its vertices, reverses precisely its chosen
canonical functional, and preserves x^2+xy+y^2. Absolute determinant one
therefore proves each specified bisection of the ellipsoidally rounded
middle fiber, without implying bisection in other directions.

The endpoint reflection pairs their two cap traces for every threshold.
The middle base is zero, so its specified canonical trace is independent
of that threshold parameter. This proves the entire moving-parameter
baseline identity, which is exactly the part of the earlier proof that
used central symmetry. The strict support margin follows from the stated
Euclidean inball of the ellipse. One fixed continuous affine coordinate
change transfers the audited face-tube regularity to this ellipsoid.
All subsequent right-inverse, reduced-Hessian, implicit correction, and
common normalization steps use unchanged proved hypotheses.

The separate nonselected cap calculation is correct: its middle triangle
fraction is 4/9 and its total is 7/6<5/4. Thus the selected budget is not
being asserted to equal the source's maximum depth. The theorem is an
actual nonsymmetric selected-cover variation, not an extremizer theorem.

## Opposite-order four-simplex scalar crossover

The root fully read `candidate 03cc52bdd22fe702`
and ran its verifier: PASS (14112 exact checks).

The two geometric lower bounds use the earlier actual subset construction,
one shared direction and tilt, and the concentric middle-shell payment.
The vertical bounds dominate both because Gamma,lambda<=1 and h<=c.
The pointwise own-centroid comparison is used within its proved scope.

For alpha>1 the exact maximum of v^d-alpha[v-x]_+^d follows from its
unique derivative zero. The weighted average of the two certificates
cancels the endpoint volume A with weights 1/(2t) and 1-1/(2t).
Its remaining expression is exactly equation (9), yielding the proved
uniform near-plateau bound after the geometric-series estimate for 1-b^d.

In the exact optimization, minimizing the maximum of two affine functions
of A gives the clipped crossover in (11). The two resulting branches in
(12) differ by H-Z. Since (H^(1/d)+x)^d has decreasing derivative,
the remaining maximum-minus-power expression is convex in H. Its two
stationary values have the stated order, and the median followed by
clipping gives the exact minimizer, including an out-of-range crossover.
This is an exact scalar reduction. The note correctly makes no claim that
the minimized expression is nonnegative for all remaining b,d.

The new near-plateau regime is a proved bounded special case. Neither the
finite computation nor the exact reduction closes unrestricted OC.
